story.head: The Flames should pile up the shots
paras: Seattle has won both meetings this season. The Kraken (8-4-1) beat Toronto 5-4 on Wednesday, while the Flames (5-7-0) lost 4-0 to Edmonton the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kraken third (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Flames sixth (tied for 27th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Kraken’s record (.654) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.435), largely thanks to their finishing. The Flames’ record (.417) is about what their chances are worth. If the Kraken’s record were closer to their chances, like the Flames’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Kraken roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). Calgary has scored 2.33 goals a game, the third fewest in the league, and allowed 3.75, the third most. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Chandler Stephenson (2 G / 9 A / 11 P in 13 GP) leads the Kraken in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Calgary. Frédérick Gaudreau (6 G / 3 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (4 G / 4 A / 8 P in 12 GP) has a team-high four goals.

Philipp Grubauer (5-1-1 / .898 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to go for Seattle. Dustin Wolf (1-4-0 / .839 SV% in 5 GS) has struggled for Calgary so far, but is expected to start. Wolf has a .855 save percentage in six starts against the Kraken, well under his usual .902. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against McMann, Beniers and Eberle.
